## Create Table for Regressions

### Helper Functions

```{python}
def county_average(df, include_cols = None):
    if "county_id" not in df.columns:
        raise ValueError("No `county_id` column found.")

    if include_cols is None:
        include_cols = [
            col for col in df.columns
            if col != "county_id" and is_numeric_dtype(df[col])
        ]
    else:
        non_num_cols = [
            col for col in include_cols 
            if col =="county_id" or not is_numeric_dtype(df[col])
            ]
        if non_num_cols:
            raise ValueError(f"Only numeric columns are allowed in `include_cols`. Non-numeric columns: {non_num_cols}")

    # Since there are no years for datacenters, take average of all years for each county
    out_df = (df[["county_id"] + include_cols].groupby("county_id", as_index = False).mean())

    return out_df
```

```{python}
def combine_dfs(base_df, dfs_to_join):
    out_df = base_df.copy()

    for i, df in enumerate(dfs_to_join):
        if "county_id" not in df.columns:
            raise ValueError(f"No `county_id` column found in dfs_to_join[{i}]")

        # Make sure all tables only have one row per county
        dupes = df["county_id"][df["county_id"].duplicated()].unique()
        if len(dupes) > 0:
            raise ValueError(f"dfs_to_join[{i}] is not unique on `county_id`. Problematic Counties: {list(dupes)}")

        out_df = pd.merge(out_df, df, how = "left", on = "county_id", validate = "one_to_one")

    missing_summary_table = (
        out_df.isna()
        .mean()
        .sort_values(ascending = False)
        .rename("missing_share")
        .reset_index()
        .rename(columns={"index":"column"})
    )

    print("Missing Summary: \n", missing_summary_table)

    return out_df
```

### Create final table


```{python}
# Average all necessary dfs by county

final_bus_df = county_average(grouped_bus_df, include_cols = ["tot_employee_count", "annual_payroll", "tot_establishment_count"])
final_gdp_df = county_average(gdp_df, include_cols = ["real_gdp_2017_dollars_thousands", "quantity_index_gdp"])
final_inc_df = county_average(inc_df, include_cols = ["personal_income_thousands_of_dollars"])
final_pop_df = county_average(pop_df, include_cols = ["population"])
final_perm_df = county_average(perm_df, include_cols = ["all_permits", "single_family_permits", "all_multifamily_permits"])
final_emp_df = county_average(emp_df, include_cols = ["unemployment_rate"])
```



### Clean up final table


## Linear Regressions

### Regression Function

```{python}
def run_linear_regression(df, y_col, x_cols):
    all_cols = [y_col] + x_cols
    reg_df = df[all_cols].dropna().copy()

    X = reg_df[x_cols]
    y = reg_df[y_col]

    X = sm.add_constant(X)

    # Linear Regression Model
    model = sm.OLS(y, X).fit()

    fitted = model.fittedvalues
    resid = model.resid

    print(model.summary())

    # Examine Residuals
    plt.figure(figsize=(7, 5))
    plt.scatter(fitted, resid, alpha=0.6)
    plt.axhline(0, color="red", linestyle = "--")
    plt.xlabel("Fitted values")
    plt.ylabel("Residuals")
    plt.title("Residuals vs Fitted Values")
    plt.show()

    # Check For Normal Distribution
    plt.figure(figsize=(7, 5))
    probplot(resid, dist = "norm", plot = plt)
    plt.title("Q-Q Plot of Residuals")
    plt.show()

    # Check VIF
    vif_df = pd.DataFrame({
        "variable": X.columns,
        "vif": [
            np.nan if col == "const" else variance_inflation_factor(X.values, i)
            for i, col in enumerate(X.columns)
        ]
    })

    print(vif_df)

    return model
```

### Regressions and Analysis

#### Air Quality

```{python}
run_linear_regression(final_df, "pm25_mean_daily_avg", ["data_center_count", "population", "tot_establishment_count_per_capita", "real_gdp_2017_dollars_thousands_per_capita", "personal_income_thousands_of_dollars_per_capita", "all_permits_per_capita"])
```

Air Quality Analysis: 

* Overall Adj. R-squared of the model is 0.243
* Data centers have a high p-value and thus are not statistically significant in this model
* The residuals are not closely centered on 0, and seem to form a vertical band towards the middle of the x-axis, indicating heteroskedasticity. Additioanlly, there are several major outliers.
* The Q-Q plot indicates approximate normality in the center, but there are some departures from normality towards the tails
* All VIFs are very low, indicating that multicollinearity is not a concern here.

#### GDP Index

```{python}
run_linear_regression(final_df, "quantity_index_gdp", ["data_center_count", "population", "unemployment_rate", "tot_employee_count_per_capita", "personal_income_thousands_of_dollars_per_capita", "tot_establishment_count_per_capita"])
```

GDP Index Analysis:

* Overall Adj. R-squared of the model is 0.084
* Data centers have a high p-value and thus are not statistically significant in this model
* Residuals are densely clustered around a single point indicating heteroskedasticity, and there are very high outliers
* The Q-Q plot shows strong departures from normality
* All VIFs are very low, so there is not high multicollinearity

#### Residential Construction Permits

```{python}
run_linear_regression(final_df, "all_permits_per_capita", ["data_center_count", "population", "pm25_mean_daily_avg", "unemployment_rate", "tot_employee_count_per_capita", "tot_establishment_count_per_capita", "real_gdp_2017_dollars_thousands_per_capita", "personal_income_thousands_of_dollars_per_capita"])
```

Establishment Analysis:

* Overall Adj. R-squared of the model is 0.108
* Data centers have a p-value of 0.003 and thus **are** statistically signficant at the 0.01 level
* Residuals form a clustered wedge shape indicating heteroskedasticity, and there are some large outliers
* The Q-Q plot shows strong departures from normality on the upper tail, but is relatively normally distributed towards the bottom and middle
* All VIFs are very low, so there is not high multicollinearity
